subject: science
promptStrong: Give me a challenging KS3 exam-style question on {lo}, then mark my answer.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for KS3 simply, with a worked example and the most common mistake.
learningObjectives: Energy changes on changes of state

questions.q: What does an exothermic reaction do to the surroundings?
options: Takes in heat, so the temperature falls
Gives out heat, so the temperature rises
questions.explain: Exothermic reactions give out (release) heat to the surroundings, so the temperature rises. Think 'exo' = 'exit' — heat exits the reaction.

questions.q: What happens to the temperature during an endothermic reaction?
options: It rises because heat is given out
It falls because heat is taken in
It rises because heat is taken in
questions.explain: Endothermic reactions take in heat from the surroundings, so the surroundings cool down and the temperature falls. 'Endo' = 'into' — heat goes into the reaction.

questions.q: A student mixes two liquids and the thermometer reading rises from 20 °C to 34 °C. What kind of reaction is this?
options: Endothermic, because heat is taken in
Exothermic, because heat is given out
questions.explain: The temperature rose, which means heat was released to the surroundings. Giving out heat makes the reaction exothermic.

questions.q: During a reaction the temperature drops from 22 °C to 8 °C and the beaker feels cold. This reaction is:
questions.explain: The temperature fell and the beaker felt cold because heat was taken in from the surroundings. Taking heat in is endothermic.

questions.q: Which of these everyday changes is exothermic?
options: An instant cold pack for an injury
questions.explain: Burning (combustion) gives out heat, so it is exothermic. Cold packs, melting and evaporating all take heat in.

questions.q: A hand-warmer gets hot when you activate it. This tells you the reaction inside is:
options: Exothermic, because it gives out heat
Endothermic, because it gives out heat
questions.explain: The hand-warmer gives out heat and feels hot, so the reaction is exothermic. Heat is being released to your hands.

questions.q: What happens to energy when chemical bonds are broken?
questions.explain: Breaking bonds always needs energy to be taken in (supplied). Making new bonds is what releases energy.

questions.q: What happens to energy when new chemical bonds are made?
questions.explain: Making new bonds releases (gives out) energy. Breaking bonds is the step that takes energy in.

questions.lo: Energy changes on changes of state
questions.q: When a solid melts to become a liquid, energy is:
questions.explain: Melting spreads the particles out more, so energy has to be taken in from the surroundings. Freezing gives energy out.

questions.lo: Energy changes on changes of state
questions.q: Steam condensing on a cold window is a change of state. During condensing, energy is:
questions.explain: Going from gas to liquid (condensing) gives energy out to the surroundings, which is why the window warms up slightly.

questions.q: Which of these is a common exothermic reaction you meet in the lab?
options: Dissolving a cold pack chemical in water
questions.explain: Neutralisation (acid + alkali) gives out heat, so it is exothermic. Thermal decomposition needs heat put in, so it is endothermic.

questions.q: Thermal decomposition means heating a substance to break it down. This process is:
options: Exothermic, because heat is given out
Endothermic, because heat must be taken in
Exothermic, because a new substance forms
questions.explain: Thermal decomposition needs energy to be supplied continuously to break the substance apart, so it is endothermic.

questions.q: In a reaction, making the new bonds releases MORE energy than breaking the old bonds took in. Overall the reaction is:
questions.explain: If making bonds releases more energy than breaking bonds needed, there is spare energy given out as heat, so the reaction is exothermic overall.

questions.q: In an exothermic reaction, energy seems to appear from nowhere. Where did it actually come from?
options: It was created by the reaction
It was already stored in the chemical bonds
It was made from nothing at all
questions.explain: Energy is never created or destroyed. The energy released was already stored in the chemical bonds and is simply transferred to the surroundings.

questions.q: Three of these give out heat. Which one is endothermic?
options: Burning natural gas on a hob
questions.explain: An instant cold pack takes heat in from the surroundings, so it feels cold — that is endothermic. Burning, respiration and neutralisation all give heat out.

questions.q: A student says: 'Exothermic means the reaction gets colder.' What is wrong with this?
options: Exothermic means heat exits, so the surroundings get warmer, not colder
questions.explain: This is a common mistake. 'Exo' means heat exits the reaction to the surroundings, so the surroundings get warmer and the temperature rises. It is endothermic reactions that feel cold.
